```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Initial ideas:
- Football scores are counts. Use some sort of Poisson regression model
- Two models: one predicting home team scores, the other away team score
- One model combining the two above to make a final prediction.
- Clustering teams based on historical performance?
- Covariates:
  - Team strength:
    - Historical goals scored
    - Recent performance
    - Opponent strength
    - Home advantage
    - Matches played and rest time
  - Team variations:
    - Squad turnover
    - Experience
    - Previous season goals/League performance
    - Some sort of metric for new players
  - Individual player stats:
    - Premier League history
    - Age
    - Position
    
- For new players who have not played before, use a technique for dealing with missing data to get a "strength score" for that player.
- Assign each player a score based on FPL data, and see how that score changes over the years (is there a trend?) so then the model will predict that score for the next year. 
- Compare scores of different positions in any match and get an overall team score (defense and attack?)
- Make a model which predicts match outcomes based on these scores (Poisson?, Cubist?)
